examples.ko: 이 자리에서 특정 회사를 거명하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to name a specific company here.
The host called out the winners one by one.
The person named in the article apologized right away.
If you mention that name, the mood gets awkward.

examples.ko: 도와준 분들을 모두 거명할 수는 없지만 감사해요.
examples.en: I can't name everyone who helped, but thank you all.
The staff were happy because I praised them by name.

explain: 사람이나 단체의 이름을 직접 말한다는 뜻이라 공식적인 자리, 기사, 연설에서 잘 어울려요. 친구끼리는 '이름을 말하다'라고 해도 돼요. '이름을 거명하다'보다 '~을/를 거명하다'로 쓰는 것이 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: That person is being named as a candidate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어의 피동형으로, 이름이 사람들 사이에서 말해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when a name comes up in discussion.

phrases.example: 그는 끝내 그 회사를 거명하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: He never named that company in the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름을 직접 말하지 않을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for not saying a name directly.

phrases.en: With a friend you can just say the name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday way to say it in conversation.

explain_en: It means saying a person's or group's name outright, so it fits formal settings, articles and speeches. Among friends you can just say '이름을 말하다'. It is more natural as '~을/를 거명하다' than '이름을 거명하다'.

examples.en: A police mobile unit was deployed to the protest site.

examples.ko: 기동대는 큰 행사에서 질서를 지키는 일을 해요.
examples.en: The mobile unit keeps order at large events.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 군대 대신 경찰 기동대에서 복무했어요.
examples.en: My uncle served in a police mobile unit instead of the regular army.

examples.ko: 축제 날에는 기동대 버스가 길가에 줄지어 서 있었어요.
examples.en: On the festival day, riot-control buses were lined up along the road.
The mobile unit members quickly cleared the accident scene.

examples.ko: 기동대에 들어가려면 체력 시험을 통과해야 해요.
examples.en: To join the mobile unit, you have to pass a physical test.

explain: 빠르게 움직여 현장에 투입되는 부대라서, 뉴스에서 '경찰 기동대'처럼 시위나 큰 행사 이야기에 나와요. 일상 대화보다는 기사에서 만나는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The members of the mobile unit are lined up and waiting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기동대에서 일하는 개개인을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the individual people who serve in the unit.

phrases.en: The police sent a mobile squad to the scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건이나 큰 행사에 부대를 보낸다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in the news for sending a unit to an incident or big event.

phrases.en: Hearing the news, the squad was dispatched right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기동대가 현장으로 급히 나간다는 뜻으로 기사에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the squad heads out to the scene quickly; common in news articles.

explain_en: This is a unit sent quickly to the scene, so it shows up in the news as '경찰 기동대' in stories about protests and big events. You meet it more in articles than in daily conversation.

examples.ko: 팔십 세 마라톤 선수가 노익장을 과시했어요.
examples.en: An eighty-year-old marathon runner showed off his vigor in old age.
Everyone was surprised at Grandfather's vigor despite his age.
Climbing mountains even at seventy, your vigor in old age is amazing.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 노익장으로 영화를 계속 찍고 있어요.
examples.en: That actor keeps making movies with the energy of someone much younger.
Elderly people who show off their vitality exercise in the park.

examples.ko: 노익장이라는 말처럼 그분은 나이를 잊고 일하세요.
examples.en: As the word 'vigor in old age' says, that person works as if age were nothing.

explain: 나이가 많은데도 힘이 넘치고 활동적인 사람을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 주로 '노익장을 과시하다'로 쓰고, 남에게 하는 말이라 자기 자신에게 쓰면 자랑처럼 들릴 수 있어요. 뉴스에서 스포츠 선수나 배우를 소개할 때 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 칠십 대 배우가 액션 장면에서 노익장을 보여 줬어요.
phrases.en: The actor in his seventies showed vigor in his old age in the action scenes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이 든 사람이 힘차게 활동하는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an older person is active and full of energy.
phrases.en_equiv: to show vigor in old age

phrases.example: 구십 세에 등산을 하시다니 노익장이 대단하세요.
phrases.en: Climbing mountains at ninety, your vigor in old age is amazing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이 든 분의 힘을 칭찬하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment on an older person's energy.

phrases.example: 그 노익장 선수는 예순 살이 넘어서도 우승했어요.
phrases.en: That veteran athlete won a title even after turning sixty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이가 아주 많아도 뛰어난 활약을 하는 선수를 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce an athlete who excels despite very advanced age.

explain_en: It is a word of praise for someone who is old but still full of energy and active. It is mostly used as '노익장을 과시하다', and since it is said about others, using it for yourself can sound like bragging. You often see it in news about athletes or actors.

examples.ko: 그분은 너무 대단해서 아무도 범접하지 못해요.
examples.en: That person is so great that nobody can come close.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 실력에는 아무도 범접할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Nobody can match that player's skill.

examples.ko: 범접하기 어려운 분위기에 말을 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: The atmosphere was so intimidating that I couldn't speak to them.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 너무 멋있어서 범접할 수 없는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: That actor is so cool that he feels unapproachable.

examples.ko: 그 요리사는 아무도 범접할 수 없는 경지에 올랐어요.
examples.en: That chef has reached a level no one else can approach.

examples.ko: 처음에는 선배가 범접하기 힘든 사람 같았어요.
examples.en: At first, my senior seemed like someone hard to approach.

explain: 거의 항상 '범접할 수 없다', '범접하기 어렵다'처럼 부정이나 어려움과 함께 써요. 지위나 실력이 높거나 위엄이 있어서 가까이 다가갈 수 없다는 느낌이고, 보통 감탄이나 존경이 담겨요.

phrases.example: 그 가수의 무대는 아무도 범접할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: No one can match that singer's stage performance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 형태로, 너무 대단해서 가까이 갈 수 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form: too impressive to get near.

phrases.en: That professor is someone hard to approach.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 어렵다'로 약간 부드럽게, 다가가기 힘든 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -기 어렵다 form is a bit softer, conveying difficulty in approaching.

phrases.example: 그는 아무도 범접할 수 없는 실력을 가졌어요.
phrases.en: He has a skill no one can reach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸며서 감탄하는 마음을 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to express admiration.

explain_en: It is almost always used with negation or difficulty, as in '범접할 수 없다' or '범접하기 어렵다'. It means someone's status, skill or dignity is so high that you cannot get close, and it usually carries admiration or respect.

en: being between teacher and student; teacher-student relations

examples.en: The two are teacher and student, but they get along like friends.

examples.ko: 우리는 십 년 전부터 사제지간으로 만났어요.
examples.en: We have known each other as teacher and student since ten years ago.

examples.ko: 사제지간의 정이 깊어서 졸업 후에도 자주 연락해요.
examples.en: Their teacher-student bond is deep, so they keep in touch even after graduation.
Even between teacher and student, you should keep good manners.
I didn't know those two were teacher and student.

examples.ko: 사제지간을 맺은 지 벌써 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has already been five years since we became teacher and student.

explain: 선생님과 제자의 관계를 말해요. 일상에서는 '스승과 제자'라고도 하고, '부자지간', '모녀지간'처럼 '-지간'이 붙는 말과 같은 짝이에요.

phrases.example: 스승과 제자가 십 년 만에 다시 만났어요.
phrases.en: The teacher and student met again after ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '사제지간' 대신 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say 사제지간.

phrases.en: The professor and I are teacher and student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 사람의 관계를 소개할 때 해요체로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite-form sentence for introducing the relationship between two people.

phrases.en: Their bond as teacher and student is deep, so they keep in touch often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선생님과 제자 사이의 따뜻한 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the warm feelings between a teacher and a student.

explain_en: It describes the relationship between a teacher and a student. In daily talk people also say '스승과 제자', and it belongs to the same '-지간' (relationship between) family as '부자지간' and '모녀지간'.

examples.en: Even a small child knows that.

examples.ko: 삼척동자라도 그 정도는 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even a mere child can understand that much.

examples.ko: 삼척동자도 알 만한 거짓말을 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't tell a lie that even a child would see through.

examples.ko: 삼척동자에게 물어봐도 같은 답을 할 거예요.
examples.en: Even if you asked a small child, they'd give the same answer.

examples.ko: 이 정도 규칙은 삼척동자라도 금방 이해해요.
examples.en: Even a young child understands a rule like this right away.
It's an obvious trick that even a child could see.

explain: 거의 '삼척동자도 알다' 틀로 써서, 누구나 아는 뻔한 일을 강조해요. 상대에게 말하면 조금 비꼬는 느낌이 들 수 있어요. 어린아이를 낮춰 보는 느낌도 있어서 아이 앞에서는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: Even a child knows that much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 틀이에요. 누구나 아는 일을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern, stressing that everyone knows it.

phrases.en: That's something even a child knows, isn't it?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 말하면 비꼬는 느낌이 날 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: May sound sarcastic when said to someone.
phrases.en_equiv: a fact even a child knows

phrases.example: 삼척동자도 알 만한 일을 왜 모르세요?
phrases.en: Why don't you know something even a child would know?
phrases.nuance_ko: 뻔한 일을 모르는 사람에게 답답함을 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses frustration at someone not knowing the obvious.

explain_en: It is almost always used in the frame '삼척동자도 알다' to stress that something is obvious to anyone. Said to someone, it can sound a bit sarcastic. It also feels slightly belittling toward children, so avoid using it in front of kids.

examples.en: I watched the gate guard changing ceremony in front of the palace.
In the old days, the gate guard opened and closed the castle gate.
The gate guard's costume was really colorful.
Tourists take photos with the gate guard.
Our team's goalkeeper is a reliable guardian of the goal.
I asked the gate guard for directions.

explain: 조선 시대에 궁궐이나 성문을 지키던 관리를 말해요. 지금은 경복궁 같은 곳의 '수문장 교대식'이 유명하고, 스포츠 기사에서는 골키퍼를 '골문을 지키는 수문장'이라고 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I watched the guard-changing ceremony at Gyeongbokgung.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관광지에서 가장 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation at tourist sites.

phrases.example: 궁궐 수문장들이 옛날 옷을 입고 서 있어요.
phrases.en: The palace gate guards stand in traditional clothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 궁궐 문을 지키는 사람이라고 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear it is a guard of the palace gate.

phrases.en: That goalkeeper is our team's guardian of the goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠에서 골키퍼를 멋있게 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A stylish metaphor for a goalkeeper in sports.

explain_en: It was the officer who guarded palace or castle gates in the Joseon era. Today the 'gate guard changing ceremony' at places like Gyeongbokgung is well known, and sports articles sometimes call a goalkeeper the '수문장' of the goal.

examples.en: I looked down on my opponent and lost badly.
Don't look down on me just because I'm young.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 사람들을 얕잡는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: That person has a habit of looking down on people.
They seem to have looked down on me because I'm new.
If you underestimate our team, you'll get burned.

examples.ko: 적을 얕잡으면 안 된다고 코치님이 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: The coach said we must not underestimate the opponent.

explain: 대부분 '얕잡아 보다' 형태로 써요. '얕보다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 상대의 힘이나 실력을 실제보다 낮게 보다가 낭패를 볼 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I took the test lightly and got a low score.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 얕봤다가 안 좋은 결과가 생겼다는 뜻으로 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say that underestimating something in the past led to a bad result.

phrases.example: 친구가 나를 얕보는 것 같아서 기분이 나빴어요.
phrases.en: I felt bad because it seemed my friend looked down on me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '얕잡다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 더 짧아서 일상에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 얕잡다, but shorter and common in daily speech.

phrases.en: You shouldn't underestimate your opponent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심하라고 충고할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving advice to be careful.

explain_en: It is mostly used in the form '얕잡아 보다'. It means almost the same as '얕보다'. It fits cases where you rate someone's strength or ability lower than it really is and then get caught out.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 파출소에는 여경이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are two policewomen at our neighborhood police box.
A policewoman helped me when I got lost.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 여경이 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to be a policewoman since I was little.

examples.ko: 여경 채용 시험에 지원한 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who applied for the policewoman hiring exam.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 여경이 범인을 쫓는 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a scene in a drama where a policewoman chases a criminal.
I asked a policewoman for directions at the event.

explain: 남자 경찰은 보통 그냥 '경찰'이라고 하고, 여자 경찰을 따로 말할 때 '여경'이라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 '경찰관님'을 써요. 뉴스와 기사에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I asked a policewoman for directions on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여경'과 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 조금 더 풀어 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 여경, spelled out a bit more in speech.

phrases.en: My older sister wants to become a policewoman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 직업을 갖는다는 뜻으로 꿈이나 목표를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a dream or goal of getting that job.

phrases.en: When you are scared, ask a policewoman for help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움이 필요할 때 부탁하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking for help in a tough situation.
phrases.en_equiv: to ask a policewoman for help

explain_en: Male officers are usually just called 경찰, and 여경 is used when you single out a woman officer. When addressing one directly, you use 경찰관님. You see 여경 often in news and articles.

en: to flock together like birds of a feather

examples.en: It's natural for similar people to gather together.

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구들은 취미가 비슷해서 유유상종해요.
examples.en: My classmates have similar hobbies, so birds of a feather flock together.
People tend to flock with their own kind and gather in similar groups.
They say birds of a feather flock together, and you two have the same personality.

examples.ko: 유유상종하다 보면 새로운 사람을 만나기 어려워요.
examples.en: If you only stick with your own kind, it's hard to meet new people.
People with the same tastes hang out together, like with like.

explain: 성격이나 취향이 비슷한 사람끼리 모일 때 쓰는 사자성어예요. 말할 때는 '유유상종이네요'처럼 감탄하듯 쓰기도 하고, 비꼬는 말투가 되기도 해요. 비슷한 한국어 표현으로 '끼리끼리 논다'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 두 사람 다 낚시를 좋아하다니 정말 유유상종이네요.
phrases.en: Both of them love fishing—birds of a feather indeed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 사람들이 모인 것을 보고 감탄하듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when you notice similar people have gathered, like a remark of amusement.

phrases.en: As they say, birds of a feather—those two have the same personality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속담처럼 앞에 놓고 그 말이 맞았다고 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed first like a proverb, then followed by a remark that it proved true.
phrases.en_equiv: just as they say, birds of a feather

phrases.en: Friends with the same hobbies hang out together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '유유상종하다' 대신 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday alternative to '유유상종하다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to hang out with one's own kind

explain_en: This four-character idiom is used when people with similar personalities or tastes group together. In speech it is often used like an exclamation, '유유상종이네요', and it can also sound sarcastic. A similar Korean expression is '끼리끼리 논다'.

examples.ko: 그는 의협심이 강해서 약한 사람을 도와요.
examples.en: He has a strong sense of chivalry, so he helps the weak.
Out of a chivalrous spirit, I stepped into the fight.
The boy showed his gallantry and saved his friend.
I want to be a person with a chivalrous heart.
I'm proud of my older brother, who is full of chivalry.
Burning with a sense of justice, he chased after the thief.

explain: 정의감과 비슷하지만, 어려운 사람을 직접 나서서 돕는 용감한 마음이라는 느낌이 더 강해요. '의협심이 강하다/있다/넘치다', '의협심을 발휘하다'로 써요.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 의협심이 강해서 어려운 사람을 그냥 못 지나쳐요.
phrases.en: My friend has a strong sense of chivalry and can't just pass by someone in need.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격을 말할 때 가장 흔히 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for describing a person's character.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a strong chivalrous spirit

phrases.en: He showed his chivalrous spirit in a dangerous situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 행동으로 도왔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone actually acts to help.

phrases.en: That boy is full of chivalrous spirit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의협심이 아주 많다고 강조할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress an abundance of chivalrous spirit.

explain_en: It is similar to a sense of justice, but it feels more like a brave heart that steps forward to help people in trouble. It is used as '의협심이 강하다/있다/넘치다' and '의협심을 발휘하다'.
